L279: ## 3 The Endomorphism Condition in $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$
L280: 
L281: In this section, we reduce the problem of describing all endomorphisms of $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ to determining when a product of two idempotents in $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ is again an idempotent. If we have resolved this problem, we can follow the procedure described in this section to obtain a concrete Boolean matrix monoid that is isomorphic to $\mathrm{End}(\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta})$.
L282: ### 3.1 $(\Theta,p)$-pure Sequences
L283: 
L284: For $X,Y\in A_{\Theta}$, we define the predicate $p(X,Y)$ by
L285: 
L286:  | $$p(X,Y):\!\iff e_{X}e_{Y}\text{ is an idempotent in }\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}.$$  |
L287: 
L288: Formally, $p$ depends on the graph $\Theta$, but we omit this dependency. For example, if $\Theta$ is the empty graph, then $A_{\Theta}=\mathbbm{2}^{[n]}$ and any product of two idempotents in $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ is again an idempotent. Hence $p(X,Y)$ holds for all $X,Y\in A_{\Theta}$ in this case.
L289: By Proposition cite42†2.9 , for all sets $X,Y\in A_{\Theta}$, we have
L290: 
L291:  | $$p(X,Y)\iff e_{X}e_{Y}\text{ is an idempotent in }\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}\iff X\cup Y\in A_{\Theta}\text{ and }e_{X}e_{Y}=e_{X\cup Y}.$$  |  | (3)
L292: ###### Theorem 3.1.
L293: 
L294: A map $\varphi:\{x_{1},x_{2},\dots,x_{n}\}\to\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ extends to a monoid endomorphism of $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ if and only if there exist sets $X_{1},X_{2},\dots,X_{n}\subseteq[n]$ such that, for all $i,j\in[n]$, the following conditions hold:
L295: 
L296:   1. (i)
L297: 
L298: $X_{i}\in A_{\Theta}$;
L299: 
L300:   2. (ii)
L301: 
L302: $\varphi(x_{i})=e_{X_{i}}$;
L303: 
L304:   3. (iii)
L305: 
L306: $p(X_{i},X_{j})$ and $p(X_{j},X_{i})$ hold if $i$ and $j$ are not connected;
L307: 
L308:   4. (iv)
L309: 
L310: $p(X_{i},X_{j})$ holds if $i\to j$.
L311: ###### Proof.
L312: 
L313: Assume that the map $\varphi$ extends to an endomorphism of $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$, which we also denote by $\varphi$. Since a monoid homomorphism maps idempotents to idempotents, $\varphi(x_{i})$ is an idempotent in $\mathrm{HK}_{\Theta}$ for all $i=1,2,\dots,n$. By Proposition cite41†2.5 , $\varphi(x_{i})$ is of the form $e_{X}$ for some $X\in A_{\Theta}$. Hence there exist sets $X_{1},X_{2},\dots,X_{n}\in A_{\Theta}$ such that
L314: 
L315:  | $$\varphi(x_{i})=e_{X_{i}},$$  |
L316: for all $i=1,2,\dots,n$, which proves (cite45†i ) and (cite46†ii ). Now let $i,j\in[n]$.
L317:

L319: 
L320:  | $$x_{i}x_{j}=x_{j}x_{i}.$$  |
